title: 2026-05-15-aegisworks-qbr-inference-economics-and-roadmap-kickoff
summary: QBR-style health check focused on usage trends, cost drivers, reliability incidents in the last quarter, and aligning roadmap and pilot for dedicated capacity. Action items: share detailed pricing, run a 72-hour latency/cost benchmark, share security pack, and propose pilot SLOs and rollout timeline.
next_steps: Jordan to send tiered pricing and Dedicated sizing options (by 2026-05-18)
Priya to propose benchmark plan and metrics (by 2026-05-20)
Miguel to share security pack and SOC2 artifact links (by 2026-05-17)
Schedule pilot kickoff meeting w/ AegisWorks platform team (target 2026-05-25)
action_items: Jordan Lee: Send tiered pricing + committed capacity examples:2026-05-18
Priya Natarajan: Draft 72-hour latency/cost benchmark plan w/ test prompts:2026-05-20
Miguel Santos: Share security package (SOC2 report, KMS integration notes, audit log examples):2026-05-17
Liam O'Connor: Provide current traffic shape + spike window logs for benchmarking:2026-05-19
transcript: 00:00:00 Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. Agenda—quick health check, cost and usage, reliability incidents, then roadmap and pilot. 00:00:12 Dana Park: Hi Jordan, thanks. We losed a few folks, but this is Dana, Liam and Sofia here. 00:00:20 Jordan Lee: Great, thanks. Quick intro from our side — Priya is our SE, Miguel our CSM. 00:00:30 Priya Natarajan: Hey all. 00:00:32 Sofia Ruiz: Hi. 00:00:35 Jordan Lee: Okay, first slide — usage trend. We saw tokens up ~38% q/q for your inference calls. Does that match what you expect, Dana? 00:00:48 Dana Park: Yeah that jibes. We launched the chat assistant in February so the q/q bump is from the new flows, and also some heavier multi-turn sessions. 00:01:00 Liam O'Connor: Most of the increase is in the embeddings and re-rank microservices during peak hours, the batch jobs in the evening. 00:01:12 Jordan Lee: Understood. On cost, I wanted to call out two drivers — longer sequence lengths pushing compute, and KV cash warm-ups — sorry, KV cache warm-ups are incurring extra tokens and latency. 00:01:28 Priya Natarajan: (laughs) KV cash — yes, the transcript engine sometimes hears cash. Real is KV cache, and we're seeing ~20% of requests hit cold cache due to short lived sessions. 00:01:39 Dana Park: We have a 30-minute session TTL right now, might be too short. 00:01:45 Jordan Lee: Right. For economics, we suggested a couple levers: prefix caching tweaks, batching config for non-latency critical endpoints, and a quantization profile for your lower-variance models. 00:01:58 Sofia Ruiz: Can you remind us about the Dedicated vs Hosted numbers? We need a ballpark for committed spend to justify to finance. 00:02:06 Jordan Lee: Sure. High level: hosted is usage-based, good to start; Dedicated is reserved capacity with predictable unit costs. I'll send a tiered pricing sheet. Example — 4x A100-equivalent reserved gives you X tokens per dollar vs hosted Y per dollar, roughly a 20–35% unit saving depending on profile. I'll put actual table in the doc. 00:02:30 Sofia Ruiz: That variance is big, 20–35% — what's the break-even timeline? 00:02:36 Jordan Lee: Depends on your steady state—if your baseline daily tokens exceed the committed capacity threshold for three months, Dedicated tends to pay off. We'll include a break-even calc in the sheet. 00:02:48 Liam O'Connor: On reliability, we had that one incident two weeks ago — a short regional outage and fallback to a smaller model increased tail latency. Can we dig into runbook and automatic fallback? 00:03:00 Miguel Santos: Yep, we correlated that. There was a routing blip to the secondary AZ and a fallback policy routed to a smaller variant which increased token count per response due to formatting differences. We've flagged an improvement to the routing policy and ensuring consistent model format to avoid token bloat when falling back. 00:03:19 Priya Natarajan: Also want to note caching can mitigate that — if prefix cache is warmed, fallback impact is much smaller. 00:03:27 Dana Park: For compliance, our security team needs to see evidence of KMS integration, SSO/SAML options, and the SOC2 report. 00:03:36 Miguel Santos: We'll send the security pack. Attached links will include SOC2, diagram of VPC private deployment, KMS/HSM notes, and audit log samples. 00:03:47 Jordan Lee: On data residency, any constraints? 00:03:50 Liam O'Connor: We're US-first but have EU customers, so we need regional routing for EU workloads and a plan to keep EU data in EU. 00:03:59 Priya Natarajan: We support region pinning and private deployments; for strict residency we'd recommend Private VPC with customer-managed networking. 00:04:08 Dana Park: Costs for Private — how different? 00:04:10 Jordan Lee: Private has higher fixed fees for the control plane and optional on-prem packaging; Dedicated is somewhere in between. We'll show comparative cost lines in the pricing doc. 00:04:19 Sofia Ruiz: Ok, finance wants the numbers in a single workbook, with three scenarios: conservative, expected, and aggressive. 00:04:26 Jordan Lee: We'll produce that. Priya, can we also propose model quantization options? 00:04:31 Priya Natarajan: Yes — we recommend q4_0 for your medium models and int8 for the low-variance embedder; it should lower GPU utilization about 15–25% depending on throughput. We'll include suggested test vectors. 00:04:44 Liam O'Connor: For benchmarking, we need a plan that mirrors production traffic — spiky windows and multi-tenancy. We can share logs. 00:04:52 Priya Natarajan: Proposed benchmark: 72-hour run, with two peak windows per day mirrored from your real logs, metrics collected: p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens, error rate, tail-latency. 00:05:06 Jordan Lee: Perfect. We'll capture that as a deliverable. 00:05:12 Dana Park: On rollout, our internal success criteria: sub-200ms p95 for 1-2 turn chat, cost per 1k tokens under $X (TBD), and no more than 0.1% request error rate. 00:05:24 Jordan Lee: We'll help define exact SLO numbers in the pilot kickoff. 00:05:29 Sofia Ruiz: One procurement note — we'll need contract language around data deletion and audit rights. 00:05:34 Miguel Santos: Noted, legal will provide standard clauses and we can iterate. 00:05:39 Liam O'Connor: A question — do you support per-route quotas and token-level cost visibility? 00:05:44 Priya Natarajan: Yes, our Console exposes per-route costs and token breakdowns, and you can set per-route quotas and alerts. 00:05:53 Dana Park: Another ops question: on-call handover — if we run Dedicated or Private, how does on-call work? 00:05:59 Miguel Santos: For Dedicated we offer an SLA-backed support package with 24/7 escalation paths; Private has options for managed on-call or ship-your-own with playbooks. We'll include an ops-runbook sample. 00:06:12 Jordan Lee: Any competitors you're evaluating? 00:06:15 Dana Park: We're looking at Anthropic's infra and some use of Vertex AI for batch embedds — but the gap is the production-grade runtimes and the tooling. 00:06:26 Jordan Lee: Good to know. We'll highlight where Redwood fits on observability and cost controls. 00:06:32 Sofia Ruiz: Can you also include a sample canary rollout plan? Our deploy windows are tight. 00:06:37 Priya Natarajan: We'll include canary/A-B templates and automatic fallback policies. 00:06:42 Liam O'Connor: For the pilot timeline — we need it to finish before fiscal close; target date end of June. 00:06:49 Jordan Lee: That gives us six weeks — doable. We'll propose a 4-week smaller internal pilot then a 2-week scale test. 00:06:58 Dana Park: Sounds reasonable. 00:07:02 Jordan Lee: Ok quick recap of next steps: pricing workbook, benchmark plan, security pack, pilot scope and kickoff invite. 00:07:12 Miguel Santos: I'll upload the SOC2 and KMS notes to the shared drive. 00:07:17 Sofia Ruiz: And please include finance-facing numbers for three scenarios. 00:07:20 Jordan Lee: Will do. 00:07:24 Liam O'Connor: One last bit — can we get more detail on autoscaling policies and burst capacity? When we had the spike the autoscaler took a while. 00:07:33 Priya Natarajan: We'll propose tuned autoscaler policies — faster warm-starts, pre-warming for known spikes, and burst pools for heavy windows. 00:07:44 Dana Park: ok great. Anything else? 00:07:46 Jordan Lee: Nothing from us. Thanks all, we'll follow up with the materials and get that pilot on the calendar. 00:07:55 Sofia Ruiz: Thanks. 00:08:00 [meeting signoff]
notes: Transcript includes a few mis-transcriptions (KV cash -> KV cache; embedds -> embeddings). Links referenced: pricing_workbook.xlsx, security_pack_v2.zip, benchmark_plan_draft.md (not attached in transcript).
